correctness.rationale: For each active diagonal coordinate, the normalized residual is multiplied by \(1-lpha_k\lambda_i\). Exact line search makes \(lpha_k^{-1}\) a Rayleigh quotient in \([\mu,L]\), so \(\kappa\le2\) keeps every multiplier in \([-1,1]\) and therefore every coordinate nonnegative. In two dimensions, two exact searches scale the residual by the explicitly derived \(\gamma\in[0,1)\), which makes all even and odd iterates nonnegative. For every \(\kappa>2\), the three-mode family has a second-iterate high-mode numerator converging to \(1-\kappa/2<0\). The packaged exact-rational verifier replays the displayed witness and two-dimensional identity.

value.rationale: Exact-line-search steepest descent is a canonical solver, while nonnegative coordinates are natural when unknowns represent rates, concentrations, masses, or other intrinsically nonnegative quantities. The theorem separates objective monotonicity from coordinate feasibility and gives a complete structural boundary: universal sign safety through \(\kappa=2\), unconditional safety in two dimensions, and immediate second-iterate failure in three dimensions above the boundary.
